content.title: Architecting a Complete Web Game in a Single Zero-Dependency HTML File: Inside Ennead
[HTML5] Carrom – Classic tabletop carrom board game with rigid disc physics and 3 AI difficulty levels
content.bodyMarkdown:
Hey r/webgames,

I built a browser adaptation of **Carrom**, the traditional tabletop strike-and-pocket game popular across South Asia.

Play here: https://kreeda.games/carrom/index.html

### How it plays:
* **Slingshot Striker Controls:** Position your striker along the baseline, pull back to set power and angle, and release to flick.
* **Official Rules:** 9 White pieces, 9 Black pieces, and the Red Queen. Standard queen covering rules and striker pocket foul penalties are active.
* **Rigid Disc Physics:** Implemented with continuous collision sub-stepping so fast striker shots don't clip through pieces, with mass ratios (2.2x striker mass) and corner pocket suction gravity.
* **3-Tier AI:** Easy (straight shots only), Medium (aim lines with minor variance), and Hard (calculates ghost-ball lines and restitution-corrected cushion bank shots).

No accounts, no ads, no installs—just pure vanilla canvas loading instantly.

I'd love feedback on the physics tuning (friction/drag feel) and whether Hard AI is beatable for seasoned carrom players!

content.title: I wanted a climbing game that actually simulates center-of-mass and barn-dooring, so I built Deadpoint (free browser physics climber)
content.bodyMarkdown:
Most climbing mechanics in games reduce the sport to simple stamina meters or QTEs, missing what actually makes bouldering so tense: shifting your weight, balancing off a single toe, and committing to a move before your forearms flash-pump.

Over the past few weeks, I built **Deadpoint**, a 2.5D physics-driven bouldering game focusing entirely on authentic movement mechanics.

### What went into the movement system:
- **Articulated 4-Limb Inverse Kinematics (IK):** Limb placement dynamically drags and torques the climber's torso rather than playing canned reach animations.
- **Center-of-Mass & "Barn-Door" Torque:** If your contact points are in a straight vertical line without a counter-flag (using `A`/`D` to swing out a free foot), rotational momentum will peel you off the wall.
- **The Deadpoint Window:** Launching toward a distant hold requires latching right at zero-G momentum (the deadpoint apex). Timing rings reward clean latches and penalize sloppy grabs with massive grip drain.
- **Dynos in Slow-Mo:** Big dynamic throws give you a split-second matrix-style slow down to track the target hold and position both hands.
- **Chalk & Pump Management:** Each hand has its own pump meter. You have to actively find stable rests to let go with one hand and chalk up before the crux.

### Tech Details:
The entire game runs on pure vanilla JS / Canvas without external physics engines or frameworks, packaged into a single lightweight file with procedural WebAudio for the chalk puffs, dynamic grunts, and dyno winds.

It features 6 boulder routes from V0 to V5 with Flash and Send scoring.

**Play it instantly in your browser (no downloads / no accounts):**
https://kreeda.games/deadpoint/index.html

I’d love feedback from both climbers and game feel enthusiasts: Does the flagging counterweight feel intuitive, or does it need a more forgiving rotational threshold on the overhung V4/V5 problems?

content.text:
Most people solve standard 3x3 tic-tac-toe by middle school and never touch it again. Once both players understand optimal lines, every match inevitably ends in an uninteresting draw.

The solution isn't abandoning the rules, but nesting them. In Ultimate Tic-Tac-Toe, you play across nine linked 3x3 boards. The catch is that whichever square you pick dictates the exact sub-board your opponent is forced to play on next. Winning isn't just about claiming a line; it's about steering where your opponent is allowed to move.

We built a clean, lightweight version featuring both the nested Ultimate grid and a customizable board that scales from 3x3 up to 9x9 Gomoku. It includes a Minimax AI with alpha-beta pruning for solo play, along with local pass-and-play.

Runs instantly in any browser with zero downloads and no account setup.
